thread:
sasha-oncall: FYI customers reporting p95/p99 spikes in eu1 since ~08:10 UTC. Monitoring alert shows host-level blkio/queue_depth spike.

natalie-support: Multiple customer timeouts on short chat calls (seq ~64). Sent request ids, escalated to infra.

omar-eng-sre: Looking at the cluster — p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~900ms, p99 up to ~1.1s. CPU and GPU utilization not saturated. I/O wait and blkio queue depth spiked on a subset of hosts.

deploy-bot: Rollout: cuda-driver-525 applied to eu1 at 2026-03-16T03:40Z. NVMe firmware batch applied to some hosts at 2026-03-16T04:30Z.

li-eng-runtime: We started seeing KV cache refill stalls after the driver update. Runtime observes token emission pauses ~300-800ms in repro runs.

tm-bench: Repro run against eu1-gpu-17: 200 rps short-generation. Baseline with driver 520: p99 ~180ms; with 525: p99 ~1.1s. Captured timeline (snip):

 tm-bench: ```
 [timeline] token 12 emitted
 [stall] 400ms pause
 [timeline] token 13 emitted
 [stall] 700ms pause
 ```

sasha-oncall: SSH'ed into host eu1-gpu-17 and pulled dmesg/journal. Observed nvme timeouts and blk_update_request errors:

 sasha-oncall: ```
 [ 748.123456] nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 8 timeout, completion polled
 [ 748.123459] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456 len 4096
 [ 748.123460] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=2345
 ```

omar-eng-sre: nvme-cli smart-log shows elevated media_errors and telemetry spikes on affected devices. blk-iostat indicates queue_depth peaking at ~128 (we usually cap at 64) — suggests NCQ/driver interaction changed request handling under bursts.

li-eng-runtime: Kernel softirq stats show long softirq latencies coincident with token stalls. I/O completions being delayed then backfilled -> runtime threads block waiting for KV responses -> token emission pauses.

omar-eng-sre: Hypothesis: combination of CUDA 525 driver changes + NVMe firmware produces a PCIe completion path regresssion or altered queueing semantics, amplifying tail latency for small random IO patterns used by the runtime.

natalie-support: Customers want immediate mitigation. Can we do something quick (routing, config) to reduce customer impact?

omar-eng-sre: Immediate mitigations we tried/suggest: 
 - Rollback driver on a small canary subset (observed p99 drop to ~200ms in repro).
 - Shift traffic from eu1 to usw2/other healthy regions for affected customers while we triage.
 - Apply blkio cgroup throttles to limit per-runtime queue_depth (reduced queue storms).

li-eng-runtime: Applied cgroup blkio throttle (max queue_depth ~32) on eu1-gpu-17 and redirected ~20% of traffic away. Observed p95 drop to ~140ms and p99 to ~260ms on that host. This is a stopgap.

sasha-oncall: Rollback plan: schedule driver rollback to 520 on 5 canary hosts tonight ~02:00Z. Need infra + platform sign-off.

infra-lead: +1 for canary rollback. Also please inventory which hosts had NVMe firmware applied so hardware team can correlate.

omar-eng-sre: Action items:
 - collect NVMe smart/logs and blk-iostat from all affected hosts (ostats)
 - schedule driver rollback on canary hosts and monitor p99/p95 closely
 - run focused fio small random r/w and our runtime repro to validate root cause
 - open Nvidia/ticket with Xid logs, nvme timeline, and repro steps

li-eng-runtime: I'll prototype a runtime-level hardening patch: more aggressive local KV caching and an async fallback path so slow NVMe completions don't stall token emission as badly.

natalie-support: Communicated status to impacted customers: mitigation in place, routing and throttles applied, ETA for canary rollback ~3h.

sasha-oncall: Will update thread after canary rollback or if we see regression. Thanks all :thumbsup:
